essence: Dawn sequence orders the day: surrender, stillness, restraint, twilight; two watches for muttering-and-worship, the rest as Śiva's remainder.
Letter-body enthroned as goddess: alphabet limbs from A to YA, consciousness-formed Sarasvatī supreme.
Wish-powers grant only the wished: unasked, unpiled, the mother's noble mood nourishes man's aims.
Awareness-lordship preconditions all doing, knowing, wanting: homage as highest, worlds' mother, Śiva's beloved.
Moonlight-prayer for the twice-born mind: night-lotus-opened, made to go supreme in heaven.
Direct address collapsing names into one: Umā, Ramā, Sarasvatī — you alone supreme.
Fierce-form litany gathered into surrender: formless, nameless, many-named — five-act-sporting Bhairavī.
Throbbing-in-every-body as meditation object: self-flashing answered by inward-resounding speech.

rasa.dominant: adbhuta with bhakti (wonder held in devotion)
rasa.sthayibhava: vismaya with rati (wonder with loving attachment)
rasa.justification: The body revealed as temple and alphabet as goddess: wonder at the ordinary made divine, carried by repeated address. Praise that beholds, then asks, then surrenders.

sections.FUNCTION: Sets the day in order, enthrones letters as goddess, and turns every sense-power toward surrender.
sections.KEY TERMS: brāhma-muhūrta (god's-hour as practice-gate); mātṛkā (letters as limbs); puṣṇātu (nourish as the only request); saṃvidīśa (awareness-lord as precondition); kumuda-candrikā (night-lotus-moonlight as opening); pañcakṛtya (five acts as her sport); spandase (you-throb as meditation object).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Dawn rite done, goddess enthroned, wishes bounded, awareness owned, moonlight asked, names one, forms surrendered, throbbing meditated.
sections.BOUNDARY: Nothing is explained yet; every verse addresses, nothing concludes.
sections.EXPLANATION: The day is divided before anything is said: surrender at god's hour, then stillness, restraint, twilight, two watches of work, and all the rest conducted as Śiva's remainder. Then the alphabet itself stands up as goddess — limbs lettered A to YA, consciousness-formed, winning. The wish-powers are bounded at once: only the wished, unasked and unpiled, and even that through the mother's mood. All doing, knowing, wanting is shown preconditioned on awareness herself, so homage goes to her as highest. Moonlight is asked to open the mind like a night-lotus. Many names collapse to one supreme. Fierce forms — Raudrī, Vāmā, Mahālakṣmī — gather without contradiction into surrender. And the practice lands in the body: she throbs in every body, self-flashing, and the answer to how-to-meditate is inward-resounding speech.
